svg.text: Later rungs: the same knife, new tools
Each room's verb is its idea; the model's misconception for each fails every time (§3.9)
Mixed tins (5.NF.1)
a half and a third into one tin: pick the sixths tin,
re-cut both; the 'add the tops and bottoms' tin
(fifths) fits neither
The Queue (4.NF.2)
line the buddies up by what they ordered; every queue
hides 2/5 vs 2/3 and 1/2 vs 3/8
The Size Oven (5.NF.5)
three cakes go in at once; put each where it will fit
after baking: ×3/4 shrinks, ×5/4 grows, ×4/4 stays
The Scoops (6.NS.1)
6 cups of batter, a 3/4-cup scoop: set out the moulds
first (8), then pour; every mould full, nothing left
The Hundred Tray (4.NF.6)
0.45 is four rows and five squares; line up 0.4,
0.405, 0.45 (longer is not larger)
The Recipe Book (6.RP.3)
2 scoops of flour to 1 of butter; a triple batch: 6 to
3. Adding the same amount (6 to 5) makes a flat cake
6 cups
